migration.description: Add the durable keyset index required to read every approval revision for one run without changing the execution approval table or its historical rows.
migration.release_unit_description: Phase-one execution-domain candidate following migration 00010; this migration is reserved for the Server-side approval-history read boundary.

compatibility_assessment.reason: The candidate adds an additive REST/MCP read operation and optional public approval metadata while the database migration adds only a query index; existing 00010 rows and columns remain readable without backfill.

durable_state.description: Approval history remains keyed by the existing persisted run_id, created_at and id values; the new index accelerates the run-bound keyset read and does not create or rewrite rows.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL index managed by the embedded Goose migration history. The existing execution_approvals table from 00009 and its 00010-compatible columns remain unchanged.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: Phase-one execution-domain candidate containing migrations 00009 and 00010.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Phase-one approval-history read candidate containing migration 00011.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Create one ordered index on execution_approvals(run_id, created_at, id) in the Goose transaction; no DML, backfill, column change or row rewrite is performed.

progress_signals: A fresh PostgreSQL schema is migrated through 00010 and 00011; migration history records 00011 only after the index transaction commits.
The migration is re-entered after a successful pass and the unique index name is observed exactly once.
A deliberate index-name collision makes the migration fail without recording a successful 00011 state; removing the collision permits forward re-entry and successful recognition.
An approval row created in the 00010 schema is unchanged and remains readable after 00011 through the durable approval store.
The approval read path rechecks run authorization on every page and binds opaque cursors to the requested run.
pause_points: Before applying 00011, verify the candidate source identity and PostgreSQL migration lock availability.
After the index transaction commits and before enabling approval-history reads for traffic.
If the index operation fails, stop the rollout, remove or repair the conflicting database object with a forward operation, and re-enter 00011; do not mark the candidate ready from partial state.

recovery.faulty_release_recovery: forward-repair-by-a-new-program-version-or-a-corrected-re-entry-after-the-failed-index-operation; no row backfill or historical approval rewrite is required

required_test_evidence: The PostgreSQL path from 00010 to 00011 verifies the index, migration history, old approval-row readability and unchanged persisted identity/context fields.
Re-entry after a successful 00011 pass is idempotent and leaves exactly one run-created approval index.
A deliberate 00011 index collision fails before successful recognition, and after forward cleanup the same migration re-enters and commits.

Real HTTP approval-list reads return the persisted id, revision and context for every status, link requested_event_id to the matching approval.requested event without rewriting its raw payload, and support reconnect with the same identity.

Read authorization, malformed/duplicate/cross-run cursor handling, explicit limit bounds, no-store headers and dependency failure mapping are covered without constructing database identities in the client.
